name: (2019 QC4)
assessment: At 120 meters wide and traveling at 47,197 km/h, this asteroid is a significant size but remains nearly 20 million kilometers away. There is no risk of impact today as it safely transits deep beyond our lunar orbit.

name: (2016 RT17)
assessment: This 117-meter rock is cruising at 32,154 km/h, which is quite leisurely compared to its faster orbital neighbors. Its miss distance of over 26 million kilometers ensures a completely peaceful passage with no threat to Earth's gravity well.

name: (2007 DK8)
assessment: This massive 912-meter giant is hurtling through the void at a blistering 83,613 km/h, making it today's most formidable visitor. Fortunately, it remains at a very safe distance of 47 million kilometers, posing zero danger to our planet despite its intimidating scale.
